messages:
Lina (AE): MerchantX asked for an enterprise commit plan + POC next week. They want reserved GPUs + autoscale, KMS-managed keys, and answers to the security questionnaire. Target profile: up to 2,000 RPS gen (chat + embeddings), p95 latency target <=200ms. Can SE/Infra/Pricing sync on sizing/pricing/runbook? cc @Mei @Raj @Connor @Jo
Mei (Solutions): On it. Quick clarifying Qs: which model(s) are they planning to use (7B quantized vs 70B)? steady baseline vs daily burst? average tokens per request?
Lina (AE): Good Qs — merchant says primarily chat: ~70% short prompts (~30 tokens), ~20% longer threads (~200 tokens), ~10% embeddings (~512 tokens). Peak ~2k RPS for ~2–3 hours/day, baseline ~400 RPS. Single region (us-west). They prefer an annual commit but open to options.
Connor (Pricing): Got it. High-level: rps_per_gpu varies a ton with model/quant and GPU. Rough rules: 7B q4 on A10G-ish ~250–500 rps; 70B needs x10 GPU power. Pricing paths: reserved monthly/annual commit (20–40% off) or on-demand + burst credits. Want a worked example with assumptions?
Lina (AE): Yes — merchant leaning annual. A worked example would help close the contract.
Mei (Solutions): For the POC I recommend: 1) reserve a small baseline pool to keep KV caches warm for the 400 RPS base, 2) autoscale with burst credits up to peak 2k, 3) run a KV/prefix cache warmup before peak windows. I'll sketch a short runbook.
Raj (SRE): Quick sizing back-of-envelope: assume 7B q4 model and conservative 300 rps per A10G-equivalent GPU under sustained load. Then required GPUs = ceil(2000 / 300) = 7. Recommend reserving 8 GPUs for headroom. Autoscale policy should keep min_pool=2 (for baseline), preheat_target=6 when approaching 75% utilization, and allow burst to reserved pool. Also set a request queue_depth cap (e.g., 500) to protect p95. Example autoscale snippet below:
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 2
  reserved_replicas: 8
  preheat_threshold: 0.75
  queue_depth_limit: 500
  spot_burst_pct: 20
  fallback_model: "7B-quantized"
```
Connor (Pricing): Example pricing calc (very rough): if list A10G-equivalent = $X per GPU/mo, 8 GPUs list = 8*X -> with 30% annual commit discount => ~0.7*8*X/mo. Add burst credits & observability premium (~+10%). I'll put concrete numbers into a spreadsheet. Any constraint on GPU family? A10G vs A100/H100 will change cost and rps_per_gpu.
Jo (Security): KMS note: MerchantX requires customer-managed keys (BYOK) and an exportable KMS audit trail for the POC. We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) but need to confirm key rotation policy and where logs are exported. Also need the completed security questionnaire v2 (I'll attach). Please confirm data retention/PII policies and whether POC data must be segregated from prod.
Mei (Solutions): I'll draft the POC checklist (smoke tests, KV warmup, throughput ramp, degrade-to-smaller-model test, telemetry checks). For smoke tests: run k6 load with tokenized payloads and gradient ramp to catch queuing. Sample perf test command I'll post to the repo.
Lina (AE): Next steps capture: @Connor — pricing calc (worked example) by EOD. @Raj — validate reserve count & post perf test script. @Jo — share questionnaire and required attestations. @Mei — PR POC runbook and prewarm script. I'll schedule a 30-min sync once we have numbers.
Connor (Pricing): On it. ETA 5pm PT for a spreadsheet with 3 scenarios (conservative/expected/high).
Raj (SRE): I'll validate the 300 rps assumption; will run a quick internal perf sweep tomorrow and post results + a small k6 script.
Jo (Security): I'll upload the questionnaire and a one-page KMS integration checklist here in the thread.
Mei (Solutions): Also note: if they want stricter p95 we should provision extra headroom or use a faster GPU family for the canary region. I'll annotate the runbook with tradeoffs.
Lina (AE): Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll message MerchantX to say we're on it and will follow up after your inputs.
